Hi Samuel — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: validate Integrata's routing/authorization flows with our SDKs, reproduce the 502s you saw in staging, and confirm an attack-plan to get to canary in your dev cluster.
- Tech stack you confirmed: Go backend + Node ingestion workers, running behind an NGINX reverse proxy and an internal API gateway. You mentioned both API-keys and mTLS on the gateway.

Immediate asks: 
1) Can you share a representative request and the staging nginx access + error lines around the 502? (curl or raw payload is best)
2) Confirm which Redwood endpoint you're calling (text generation vs structured_call vs embeddings) — you mentioned a structured tool-calling pipeline and an embeddings/reranker step.
3) Small sample of the payload (redact PII) and approximate average prompt length.

Connor and Marissa from our eng/tiger team are looped to own repro and a short playbook. I've attached my post-call notes.

Proposed timeline: Connor will attempt a repro in our isolated staging tomorrow, Marissa will triage any 5xx traces and propose a workaround (short-term: header/content-length/disable-streaming). If we can reproduce, we'll share a one-page KB + a small patch you can test in a canary within 48 hours.

Thanks — Aisha

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the quick recap. Per your asks below, attaching two things inline and one file: a small curl that reproduces the 502 we see in staging, and the relevant nginx error lines. I also attached a zipped log bundle to the separate link (no PII).

Quick notes from our side: 
- Endpoint: calling Redwood structured_call endpoint followed by an embeddings/reranker step in our pipeline. We do an initial call to get tool arguments, then immediately batch those items for embeddings.
- Typical request shape: large metadata block (~1.5–2k tokens) + nested structured call arguments (arrays of objects), and in some cases we batch 8 tool-calls in a single request.
- Repro: if we set batch size to 1 the 502 is intermittent but much rarer; bust to 6–8 and it becomes reliably reproducible in staging under load.

Curl (redacted API-keys): 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/structured_call 
  -H 'Authorization: ApiKey *****' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '@sample_payload.json'

nginx error excerpt: 
2027/05/03 15:58:47 [error] 31245#0: *121 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.34, server: _, request: "POST /v1/structured_call HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.2.3.45:8080/", host: "api.redwood-inference.com"

Link to log bundle: https://integrata.s3.amazonaws.com/logs/INT-034-staging-logs.tar.gz

Let us know if you want us to open a temporary vpn/ssh to staging. We'll also try lowering batch sizes and toggling streaming while you attempt reproduction.

—Sam

Subject: Re: Integrata - post-demo recap + immediate asks

Hi Sam — thanks for the logs and the curl. I pulled the sample_payload.json and ran a few quick experiments against our internal staging endpoint. A few notes and a minimal repro script attached.

Observations / quick hypotheses:
- The nginx error matches an upstream process crash or connection drop during response streaming. If the Redwood runtime opens a keepalive stream then an early socket close can cause the upstream-closed-response-header error you see.
- Two levers to quickly test: (A) disable streaming on the structured_call (stream: false) and (B) set explicit Content-Length instead of chunked transfer from your workers. Some Node HTTP clients switch to chunked when body is a stream — that can trigger proxy buffering issues.
- Batching: reduce batch size to 2 for the structured_call and run the embeddings fan-out separately — large combined requests amplify memory/timeout pressure.
- Timeouts: increase proxy_read_timeout/nginx proxy settings to 90s while we debug; you can revert after patch.

Repro steps I ran locally (attached repro script): 
1) curl -> structured_call with sample payload (batch size 6) -> observed server side task exit (OOM-like) in 2/10 runs.
2) same payload but stream=false and Content-Length set -> no upstream close in 20 runs.

Short-term playbook I'm recommending: 
- Can you toggle stream=false and add Content-Length in Node workers for a quick canary?
- Drop structured_call batch to <=2 for now, and call embeddings as separate requests (or stagger with 200ms).
- We'll push a targeted fix to better handle chunked transfer in our next runtime patch if we confirm root cause.

Attaching: integrata-repro-script.sh

I can hop on a debug session tonight PST if that's useful.

—Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Integrata - post-demo recap + immediate asks

Hi all — I reproduced the failure in our dedicated repro env this morning using Sam's payload. Attaching the trimmed trace (integrata-error-trace.txt). High-level: the runtime is crashing during response serialization when using chunked transfer with streaming enabled and large nested JSON arrays.

Key findings: 
- Stack shows early error in our serializer: java.lang.IllegalStateException: unexpected end of stream while writing chunked response -> leads to upstream close and nginx error.
- Repro is deterministic when batch >=5 and streaming enabled; toggling streaming off or adding Content-Length resolves the crash in our env.
- Root cause looks like our chunked-stream buffer mismanagement with KV-cache warmup for large embedding batches; the buffer pool was returning a null slice in rare conditions.

Temporary mitigations I tested successfully: 
1) Set streaming=false for structured_call (immediately prevents crash).
2) Force non-chunked upload (Content-Length header) at the client — avoids proxy buffering edge-case.
3) Reduce structured_call batch size to <=2 and separate embeddings.

Recommended short-term rollout plan: 
- Integrata toggles streaming=false and sets Content-Length in Node workers as a canary.
- Redwood will prepare a runtime patch that adds a defensive check in the chunked buffer allocator (target: next 48 hours).
- After runtime patch, we validate with batch=6 and streaming on in a canary cluster.

Marissa will own the patch; Connor will coordinate the canary. Aisha — happy to join a follow-up call for Exec/PM alignment.

Thanks — Marissa
